ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in parallelogram $ABCD$, $O$ is the midpoint of the diagonal $AC$, $AC\perp AB$, point $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$, and $OF\perp BC$, $\angle D=53^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle FOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram, \\
$\therefore$ AB $\parallel$ CD, AD $\parallel$ BC, \\
Since AC $\perp$ AB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BAC = $\angle$DCA = 90$^\circ$, \\
Since point O is the midpoint of AC, and point E is the midpoint of AD, \\
$\therefore$ OE $\parallel$ CD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$COE + $\angle$ACD = 180$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$COE = 90$^\circ$ \\
Since $\angle$D = $\angle$B = 53$^\circ$, and OF $\perp$ BC, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$FOC = $\angle$B = 53$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$EOF = $\angle$EOC + $\angle$FOC = 90$^\circ$ + 53$^\circ$ = \boxed{143^\circ}, \\
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, in parallelogram $ABCD$, $O$ is the midpoint of diagonal $AC$, $AC\perp AB$, point $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$, and $OF\perp BC$. If $\angle D=53^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle FOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a parallelogram, $AB\parallel CD$ and $AD\parallel BC$. Since $AC\perp AB$, $\angle BAC=\angle DCA=90^\circ$. Since point $O$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and point $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$, $OE\parallel CD$. Therefore, $\angle COE+\angle ACD=180^\circ$, so $\angle COE=90^\circ$. Since $\angle D=\angle B=53^\circ$, and $OF\perp BC$, $\angle FOC=\angle B=53^\circ$. Therefore, $\angle EOF=\angle EOC+\angle FOC=90^\circ+53^\circ=\boxed{143^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, ABCD is a slanted parallelogram, with A and D above, and B and C below; diagonal AC connects from A to C, and point O is on AC; point E is located on the upper side AD, and point F is located on the lower side BC; the figure draws the line segments from O to E and from O to F, and F and E are respectively located in the regions formed on the two sides of ray OC. Reasoning: In triangle ACD, O is the midpoint of AC, and E is the midpoint of AD, so by the midline theorem, OE∥CD. Because ABCD is a parallelogram, AB∥CD; and it is known that AC⊥AB, therefore AC⊥CD. OC is on AC, and OE∥CD, so OC⊥OE, that is, ∠EOC=90°. Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so ∠B=∠D=53°. Also because AD∥BC, and OF⊥BC; at the same time OC is on AC, and AC⊥AB, so OC⊥AB. When two straight lines are respectively perpendicular, the angle formed by them is equal to the angle formed by the original two straight lines; therefore ∠FOC is equal to the angle formed by AB and BC, that is, ∠B=53°. From the position in the figure, OE and OF are on the two sides of OC, so ∠FOE=∠FOC+∠COE=53°+90°=143°.
